summary.title: Rebuilding Git in Ruby
summary.one_liner: You learn how Git stores data internally by re-implementing its core commands (init, add, commit) as small Ruby scripts.
keywords: how git works under the hood
takeaways: Git's top-level command dispatches to separate subcommand scripts, following the UNIX small-tools convention.
git init creates a .git directory with HEAD, objects, and refs; HEAD holds a symbolic ref to the current branch.
git add hashes file contents with SHA1, stores a zlib-compressed blob under objects/, and records the SHA and path in the index.
git commit builds nested tree objects from the index, writes a commit object pointing to the root tree, and updates the current branch ref.
summary.summary: The article walks through a simplified Git clone called RGit written in Ruby, built step by step. It covers a dispatcher script for subcommands, a git init that creates the .git directory layout, and a git add that hashes and compresses file contents into objects and writes a text index. It then shows a commit step that turns the index into tree and commit objects and updates the branch ref. The author simplifies the binary index format to a text one for clarity, and the full source is linked on GitHub.
